story.title: Elephants
paragraphs_en: Elephants are the largest living land animals. They can grow as large as four metres tall and weigh as much as 6 tons. Elephants have very long trunks which they use for many different tasks.
Elephants use their trunks to help them reach their food. They are herbivores and eat fruit, leaves, trees and grass. Elephants can eat as much as 150 kilograms per day.
There are three different species of elephant: the African bush elephant, the African forest elephant and the Asian elephant. The elephants shown in this picture are African forest elephants.
Young male elephants like to play fight. This helps them to see how strong they are and learn the tactics that they will need when they get older.
Baby elephants are called calves. Elephant calves stay near their mothers until they learn to find food and drink with their trunks.
